snippets: This guide covers the full ASP.NET Core 10 ecosystem for building enterprise applications — from C# fundamentals through MVC, Web API, Razor
The guide is structured in ten chapters that mirror how you would learn and build a real enterprise application — starting with the language
Understanding how the pieces fit together is essential before writing code. The .NET 10 stack provides a unified platform for all applicatio
These tools are used throughout the guide. Install them once and they carry you through every chapter.
Modern C# is a rich language with features that directly improve enterprise code quality — immutability, pattern matching, null safety, and
Records provide value-based semantics for data transfer objects, domain models, and immutable configurations. They are the backbone of clean
C# pattern matching has evolved into a powerful tool for business logic, replacing complex if-else chains with expressive, compiler-checked
Nullable reference types eliminate null reference exceptions at compile time. Every enterprise project should enable this feature.
Async is not just about performance — it is about writing correct, scalable I/O-bound code. Understanding the internals prevents deadlocks a
LINQ is the primary data manipulation tool in C#. Understanding deferred execution, projection, and aggregation is essential for writing eff
Generics enable type-safe, reusable components. Enterprise applications rely heavily on generic repositories, services, and middleware.
ASP.NET Core is built on a composable middleware pipeline with first-class dependency injection. Understanding these fundamentals is critica
The Program.cs file is the entry point. With .NET 10, the minimal hosting model is the recommended approach for new projects.
Middleware components form a pipeline that handles each HTTP request. Order matters — each component can short-circuit or pass to the next.
ASP.NET Core has a built-in DI container. Understanding service lifetimes is essential for avoiding captive dependencies and memory leaks.
ASP.NET Core uses a layered configuration system with multiple providers. Enterprise apps need strongly-typed configuration with validation.
Environment-specific configuration and secret management are non-negotiable in enterprise applications.
The Model-View-Controller pattern is the foundation of server-rendered web applications in ASP.NET Core. It separates concerns and enables t
Controllers handle HTTP requests, orchestrate business logic, and return responses. They should be thin — delegating to services.
ASP.NET Core supports attribute routing, conventional routing, and minimal API routing. Attribute routing is preferred for APIs.
Model validation is built into ASP.NET Core via data annotations. Custom validators handle complex business rules.
Razor is the server-side templating engine. It combines HTML with C# to generate dynamic pages.
Filters run before or after action execution. They implement cross-cutting concerns like logging, caching, and error handling.
Web APIs are the backbone of modern enterprise applications. ASP.NET Core provides both controller-based and minimal API approaches.
RESTful APIs use HTTP verbs, status codes, and resource-based URLs. Following REST conventions makes APIs predictable and self-documenting.
Minimal APIs are ideal for microservices, small endpoints, and rapid prototyping. They reduce boilerplate while maintaining full DI and midd
API versioning is essential for enterprise applications with multiple clients. ASP.NET Core supports URL, header, and query string versionin
Swagger/OpenAPI is the industry standard for API documentation. ASP.NET Core integrates it seamlessly.
CORS and rate limiting are essential for public APIs. Both are built into ASP.NET Core.
Razor Pages provide a simpler alternative to MVC for page-focused scenarios. Each page is self-contained with its own model and handlers.
Razor Pages combine the view and controller into a single PageModel class. This reduces ceremony for simple CRUD pages.
Page handlers are named methods that correspond to HTTP verbs. OnGet, OnPost, OnPut, OnDelete, and custom named handlers.
PageModel is the code-behind class for a Razor Page. It handles binding, validation, and orchestration.
Layouts provide shared structure. Sections allow pages to inject content into specific layout regions.
Blazor enables building interactive web UIs with C# instead of JavaScript. It supports both server-side and WebAssembly hosting models.
Blazor Server runs components on the server and updates the DOM over SignalR. It offers fast startup and full .NET runtime access.
Blazor WebAssembly runs the .NET runtime in the browser via WebAssembly. It enables true client-side execution with offline support.
Blazor components have a well-defined lifecycle. Understanding the rendering pipeline is key to performance.
Blazor provides two-way data binding and event handling with a simple syntax.
Blazor Server requires careful state management due to its stateful nature. Use cascading values and DI scopes.

runtime access. blazor webassembly runs the .net runtime in the browser via webassembly. it enables true client-side execution with offline support. blazor components have a well-defined lifecycle. understanding the rendering pipeline is key to performance. blazor provides two-way data binding and event handling with a simple syntax. blazor server requires careful state management due to its stateful nature. use cascading values and di scopes. ef core is the primary orm for .net. it supports code-first and database-first approaches with migrations, change tracking, and linq transla dbcontext is the bridge between your domain and the database. it manages change tracking, queries, and persistence. entity configuration is done via ientitytypeconfiguration classes, keeping mapping logic organised and testable. migrations manage database schema changes over time. they are essential for team collaboration and ci/cd. ef core performance depends on understanding change tracking, query translation, and n+1 prevention. ef core supports one-to-one, one-to-many, and many-to-many relationships with fluent configuration. ef core interceptors allow you to hook into database operations for auditing, logging, and soft delete. enterprise applications need patterns that manage complexity, improve testability, and enable evolution. clean architecture, cqrs, and resil clean architecture separates concerns into layers with dependencies pointing inward. the domain has no external dependencies. cqrs separates reads and writes. mediatr implements the mediator pattern, decoupling controllers from business logic. fluentvalidation integrates with mediatr via pipeline behaviors, ensuring all commands are validated before handling. polly provides retry, circuit breaker, timeout, and fallback policies for resilient distributed systems. asp.net core provides in-memory, distributed, and response caching. choose the right strategy for each scenario. security is non-negotiable in enterprise applications. asp.net core provides built-in support for authentication, authorization, and protect jwt (json web tokens) is the standard for stateless api authentication. asp.net core supports both jwt validation and token generation. authorization policies define who can access what. they support roles, claims, and custom requirements. identity provides a complete user management system with registration, login, roles, claims, and external providers. security headers protect against xss, clickjacking, mime sniffing, and other common attacks. testing and deployment are where enterprise applications prove their worth. automated testing and containerised deployment are industry stan xunit is the standard testing framework for .net. it supports facts, theories, and async tests. integration tests verify the full stack — controllers, services, database, and middleware — working together. docker enables consistent deployment across environments. multi-stage builds keep images small. github actions provides a complete ci/cd pipeline for .net applications with testing, building, and deployment.

snippets: Static sites are written in HTML and shipped as-is. Dynamic apps generate HTML on the server or client per request. Both have a place in mod
Do not use Node.js when a static HTML file would do. Do not write raw PHP when a framework gives you routing, templating, and escaping for f
A text editor, a local server, and a terminal. For static: any editor + a static file server. For dynamic: XAMPP (PHP), Visual Studio (ASP.N
A folder of .html, .css, and .js files can become a complete website without any build step. Just open index.html in a browser.
Static site generators like Hugo, Jekyll, Astro, and Next.js in export mode generate HTML from templates and data at build time. The output
Static sites can be hosted on GitHub Pages, Netlify, Vercel, Cloudflare Pages, or any S3-compatible bucket. No server is required.
PHP is still one of the most common server-side languages. A single .php file can contain HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and SQL queries.
ASP.NET Core with Razor pages is the Microsoft equivalent of PHP templates. Each page has a .cshtml file with a page model that handles GET
